text.text: Commission lines to chase
Renewals are most of an agency's income and most of its lost clients. A steady 90-60-30 rhythm keeps both under control.
The timeline

cells.text: Pull the policy, check claims and changes in the past year, ask the client about new cars, renovations, staff or payroll
Carrier renewal offer arrives; compare it with last year's premium
If the increase is large, ask other appointed carriers for quotes
Renewal call with the client; record the decision
Signed forms and payment set up; certificates reissued for businesses
New term starts; update dates, premium and commission rate here

text.text: Step by step
Every Monday, open
Expiring in 60 days
on the Policies list.
Press
Start renewal
on each one that is still In force. It moves to Renewing.
Add a follow-up: Renewal call, due 30 days before expiry, owned by the account manager.
When the carrier offer comes in, enter the new premium on the follow-up note, not on the policy, until the client accepts.
After the call, write down what the client chose and why. If they chose to shop the policy, add a Quote follow-up.
On the first day of the new term, update the effective and expiry dates, the premium and the commission rate, and set the status back to In force.
When a client leaves
Set the policy to Lapsed, and note the reason in the follow-up: price, service, sold the car, moved, or went to another agency. A yearly look at these reasons tells you where you lose business.
Large increases
Check whether a claim, a new driver or a rate filing caused it
Ask the carrier underwriter if any credit was missed
Quote at least two other appointed carriers before the call
Explain the reason to the client in plain words
Checklist for business renewals
Payroll, revenue and headcount updated
New locations or vehicles added
Certificates of insurance reissued to everyone who holds one
Workers compensation audit questions answered
Example

Riverbend Roofing's workers compensation and liability both expire in six days. The workers compensation renewal came in 18 percent higher after the ladder-fall claim, so Rosalind is remarketing it and has a call booked with the owner before the term ends.

pages.title: Supporting an insured through a claim

text.text: The carrier pays the claim, but the client remembers how the agency helped. Your job is to report quickly, keep the file moving and keep the client informed.
When a client reports a loss
Make sure everyone is safe and the damage cannot get worse: water shut off, the car towed, the property secured.
Press
Log a claim
on the policy. Fill in the date of loss and the date it was reported.
Report it to the carrier the same day, by portal or phone. Enter the carrier claim number and adjuster name when you get them.
Tell the client what happens next and when they will hear from the adjuster.
Add a follow-up for your next check-in, usually three working days later.
What the adjuster usually needs

cells.text: Photos, repair estimates, receipts for emergency repairs
Police report number, photos, other driver's details, repair shop
First report of injury, witness names, doctor's notes
Incident report, photos of the area, names of witnesses
Police report, receipts or serial numbers

text.text: Keep it moving
A claim with no update for a week gets a call to the adjuster.
Every call goes on the claim page as a dated note: who you spoke to and what they said.
When the carrier pays, enter
Paid by carrier
and set the status to Settled.
If the carrier denies the claim, set it to Denied, keep the denial letter, and make sure the client knows their options. Do not argue coverage yourself; involve the agency principal.
What the agency must not do
Never promise a claim will be paid, never estimate what the carrier will pay, and never tell a client a loss is or is not covered. Pass coverage questions to the carrier and record that you did.
After the claim
Claims affect renewals. Add a note to the policy's renewal follow-up so the account manager expects a premium change and can explain it.
Example

The Lindqvist-Banks household reported water damage in the kitchen four days after it happened. The claim is logged with the carrier, an adjuster is not yet assigned, and Patrice has a follow-up in two days to chase the assignment.
A new client is won or lost in the first conversation. A tidy intake gets accurate quotes quickly and avoids surprises at renewal.
The first call
Ask, and write down on the insured's page:
Who and what needs insuring: drivers and vehicles, the home, the business and what it does.
Current carrier, expiry date and premium, and why they are shopping.
Claims in the past five years.
For businesses: revenue, payroll, number of employees, locations, contracts that require certain insurance.
Set it up here
Add the insured with status Prospect and choose Household or Business.
Add a policy for each line they want quoted, with status Quote, business type New business and the proposed effective date.
Add a Quote follow-up for each, due within three working days.
Note which carriers you will ask. Only ask carriers your agency is appointed with.

If they do not buy
Set the policy to Lapsed with a note on why, and add a follow-up 60 days before their current policy expires next year. Many clients come back at the next renewal.

An agency runs on habits. These routines take about an hour a week and keep the book clean.
Every Monday
Follow-ups
: clear Overdue first, then plan Due this week. Reassign anything stuck with someone who is away.
Policies
: open Expiring in 60 days and start any renewal not yet started.
Claims
: any claim with no note in seven days gets a call.
Quotes
: open quotes older than two weeks get a call or are closed.
Every Friday
Any policy still Renewing after its expiry date is an emergency: confirm with the carrier that the renewal is bound and paid, the same day.
Check that every call this week that needs action has a follow-up.
Look at the policies board: nothing should sit in Renewing past its expiry date.
Once a month: commission statements
Carriers send a statement listing what they paid on each policy. Match it line by line.
Add one line per policy on the statement under
Commission statements
, with the expected amount from the policy and the amount received.
Mark it
Received
when they match,
Short paid
when less arrived,
Chargeback
when the carrier took commission back after a cancellation or audit.
Short paid lines get a note and a follow-up to the carrier's commission department.
Expected lines older than 60 days go to the agency principal.

The Greer & Osei property installment came in at 410 dollars against 548 expected. The note says the mid-term endorsement was not paid, so a follow-up goes to the carrier and the line stays Short paid until the next statement.

This workspace is the back office of a small independent agency. The carrier systems still hold the official policy, billing and claim records; this is where the team sees the whole book at once and nothing slips between them.
What lives where

cells.text: Each household or business, the account manager, premium in force, active policies, open quotes and claims in progress
Policy number, line, carrier, term dates, days to renewal, new or renewal, billing, premium, commission rate, expected and received commission
Date of loss, carrier claim number, adjuster, amount claimed and paid
One line per policy per carrier statement, expected against received
Calls, documents, quotes and reviews someone owes, with a due date

text.text: The money columns
Premium in force
counts policies that are In force or Renewing. Quotes and lapsed policies are left out.
Expected commission
is the annual premium times the commission rate on the policy. Use the rate on the carrier's commission schedule.
Commission received
adds up lines marked Received, Short paid or Chargeback, so a taken-back commission lowers the total.
Your first week
Add your team, then enter every active policy with its number, carrier, effective and expiry dates and premium. A download from your agency system is the quickest start.
Link each policy to its insured. Households and businesses each get one record.
Fill in the commission rate for each policy from the carrier's schedule.
Enter every open claim with the carrier claim number and the adjuster's name.
Add follow-ups for any renewal inside 60 days that nobody has started.
The daily rhythm
Morning:
Follow-ups due this week and anything overdue; then Policies, Expiring in 60 days.
During the day:
every client call that needs action becomes a follow-up with a date and an owner.
End of day:
claims with no update in a week get a call to the adjuster.
Buttons you will use
Start renewal
moves a policy to Renewing.
Log a claim
and
Add follow-up
open a new linked record.
Tick done
closes a follow-up and dates it.
Assign to me
takes a follow-up over.
The workspace never decides what coverage a client needs. Record what was discussed and who decided; leave advice to licensed staff.
Example
The Halloran auto policy renews in 15 days with a higher premium. Rosalind starts the renewal, books a call about the change, and notes the client's choice on the follow-up when they speak.
